He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]] and was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a junior in 2016–17. Kuzma was selected in the first round of the [[2017 NBA draft]] with the 27th overall pick, and he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2018. He won an [[NBA championship]] with the Lakers in 2020 before being traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2021. ==Early life== Born on July 24, 1995, in [[Flint, Michigan]], Kuzma is the son of Karri Kuzma, a high school [[shot put]] champion who attended college on a track scholarship. He has a younger half-brother named Andre and a younger half-sister named Briana. Kuzma is biracial.{{Cite news |last=Ganguli |first=Tania |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Lakers report: Kyle Kuzma not afraid to tackle social issues |work=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-report-20180327-story.html |access-date=August 13, 2018}} Kuzma met his father, Larry Smith, only once as an infant, but viewed the father of his half-siblings as a father figure.{{Cite news |last=Spezia |first=Mark |date=July 28, 2017 |title=Mom's support, Flint roots buoy new Laker Kyle Kuzma's impressive summer |work=Detroit Free Press |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/2017/07/29/moms-support-flint-roots-buoy-new-laker-kyle-kuzmas-impressive-summer/512219001/ |url-status=live |access-date=August 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826150213/http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/2017/07/29/moms-support-flint-roots-buoy-new-laker-kyle-kuzmas-impressive-summer/512219001/ |archive-date=August 26, 2017}} Karri Kuzma and Smith put a toy basketball rim in the living room for Kyle when he was only two years old, thus igniting his passion for basketball.{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Ryan |date=June 5, 2017 |title=Kyle Kuzma: My Life As An NBA Draft Prospect |url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2017/06/05/kyle-kuzma-nba-draft-2017/ |access-date=December 12, 2017 |publisher=CBS}}{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Joon |date=October 5, 2017 |title='I Didn't Want to Go Back There': Lakers' Kyle Kuzma Talks About His Motivation |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2737129-i-didnt-want-to-go-back-there-lakers-kyle-kuzma-talks-about-his-motivation |access-date=August 13, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com}} Kuzma has described Flint as "a really violent place [where] there's a lot of temptation to get into the streets." However, Kuzma described basketball as his "safe haven". Kuzma attended [[Swartz Creek Community Schools]] and transferred to [[Bentley High School (Burton, Michigan)|Bentley High School]] in Michigan, where he averaged 17.9 points, 14.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 3.4 blocks per game as a junior. Kuzma sent tapes of his shooting at the YMCA to preparatory schools; Vin Sparacio, head coach at Rise Academy in Philadelphia, saw a {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|abbr=unit}}, {{Convert|175|lb|kg|abbr=in}}, raw player who had a great feel for the game, and immediately brought him in. As a high school senior at Rise Academy, Kuzma averaged 22 points and seven rebounds per game. Kuzma received offers to play with [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] schools including [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Iowa State Cyclones basketball|Iowa State]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], and [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], among others, before deciding on the [[University of Utah]]. ==College career== Kuzma enrolled at the [[University of Utah]] in 2013. He [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his freshman year due to the fact that he signed late. He became a starter for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utes]] in his sophomore year, when he averaged 10.8 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Kyle Kuzma |url=https://www.utahutes.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4142 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023010937/https://www.utahutes.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4142 |archive-date=October 23, 2017 |publisher=University of Utah Athletics}} As a junior in [[2016–17 Utah Utes men's basketball team|2016–17]], he averaged 16.4 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game, which earned him first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors.{{Cite news |date=March 6, 2017 |title=Kuzma Named to All-Pac-12 First Team |language=en |publisher=University of Utah Athletics |url=https://www.utahutes.com/news/2017/3/6/mens-basketball-kuzma-named-to-all-pac-12-first-team.aspx |access-date=May 26, 2017}} After the season, Kuzma decided to enter the [[2017 NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college basketball eligibility. Kuzma graduated from the University of Utah with a degree in [[sociology]].{{Cite news |last=Hein |first=Brett |date=May 3, 2017 |title=Utah basketball's Kyle Kuzma to hire agent, remain in NBA Draft |work=Standard-Examiner |url=http://www.standard.net/Utah-Utes/2017/05/03/Utah-basketball-Kyle-Kuzma-hire-agent-remain-in-NBA-Draft |access-date=May 26, 2017 |archive-date=October 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018072038/http://www.standard.net/Utah-Utes/2017/05/03/Utah-basketball-Kyle-Kuzma-hire-agent-remain-in-NBA-Draft |url-status=dead }}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XTNV0No9U50 |title=Why KYLE KUZMA Is The STEAL of the DRAFT |date=October 17, 2017 |publisher=BBALLBREAKDOWN |time=7:47 |access-date=November 19, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2017–2021)=== Kuzma was selected with the 27th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. However, he never played for the Nets as he was involved in a draft-day trade sending him along with [[Brook Lopez]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[D'Angelo Russell]] and [[Timofey Mozgov]].{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2017 |title=BROOKLYN NETS ACQUIRE D'ANGELO RUSSELL AND TIMOFEY MOZGOV FROM L.A. LAKERS |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/06/22/brooklyn-nets-acquire-dangelo-russell-and-timofey-mozgov-la-lakers |access-date=June 22, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} Prior to the draft, Kuzma had been projected to go in the second round.{{Cite news |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=November 14, 2017 |title=Kyle Kuzma is more than the Lakers' other rookie — he's got game |work=[[Andscape]] |url=https://andscape.com/features/nba-kyle-kuzma-lakers-rookie-lonzo-ball-hes-got-game/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115135405/https://theundefeated.com/features/nba-kyle-kuzma-lakers-rookie-lonzo-ball-hes-got-game/ |archive-date=November 15, 2017}} On July 3, 2017, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Lakers.{{Cite web |date=July 3, 2017 |title=Lakers Sign Ball, Kuzma and Hart |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170703-ball-kuzma-hart |access-date=July 4, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} During the seven games he played for the Lakers (starting in six of the games) in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], Kuzma led the team in points scored and became a consistent presence during the event. He recorded averages of 21.9 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.4 blocks, and 1.1 steals per game and was named to the All-Summer League Second Team that year. He was also named the Summer League Championship Game MVP after recording a double-double of 30 points and 10 rebounds in a 110–98 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the championship game.{{cite web|first=Joey|last=Ramirez|title=Kyle Kuzma Chosen As Summer League Championship MVP|date=July 17, 2017|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/170717-kyle-kuzma-championship-mvp|access-date=July 27, 2021}} [[File:Kyle Kuzma 2018 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Kuzma at [[Capital One Arena]] in 2018]] On November 3, 2017, in his first game as a starter, he notched his first double-double, with 21 points and 13 rebounds, in a 124–112 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2017 |title=Running Diary: Lakers vs. Nets (11/3/17) |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/171103-running-diary-lakers-nets |access-date=November 5, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} On November 17, he recorded another double-double by scoring 30 points, to go with 10 rebounds, in a 122–113 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Joey |date=November 17, 2017 |title=Kuzma Drops 30 But Lakers Can't Hold Back Suns |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/171117-postgame-wrap-lakers-suns |access-date=November 19, 2017}} Kuzma was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Western Conference Rookie of the Month]] for games played in October/November. In 20 games, he averaged a team-high 16.7 points while shooting 50.4 percent overall and a team-leading 37.9 percent on [[three-point field goal]]s. He was the first ever NBA rookie to compile at least 330 points, 120 rebounds, and 30 made three-pointers in his first 20 games.{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2017 |title=Kyle Kuzma Named Western Conference Rookie of the Month |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/171201-kuzma-rookie-of-month |access-date=December 2, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} He was also just the sixth non-[[NBA lottery|lottery]] pick to win the award in the first month of his career.{{Cite news |last=Ganguli |first=Tanya |date=December 1, 2017 |title=Lakers' Kyle Kuzma named rookie of the month, and he might play Saturday |work=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-report-20171201-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212052521/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-report-20171201-story.html |archive-date=December 12, 2017}} On December 20, he scored a career-high 38 points on 70% shooting in a 122–116 win over [[Houston Rockets|Houston]], ending the Rockets' 14-game winning streak.{{Cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Joey |date=December 20, 2017 |title=Running Diary: Lakers at Rockets (12/20/17) |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/171220-lakers-rockets-running-diary |access-date=December 21, 2017}} In the following game, Kuzma scored a game-winning three pointer to lift the Lakers to a 124–121 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]], to cap off his 25 point night.{{Cite magazine |last=Rohlin |first=Melissa |date=2020-08-10 |title=Lakers' Kyle Kuzma On Game-Winner: 'Jesus Could Be In Front Of Me And I'd Still Shoot' career playoff high 19 points in Game 3 of the [[2020 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], in a 115–104 loss against the [[Miami Heat]]. The Lakers won the series 4–2 to tie the league high with their 17th [[NBA championship]]. On December 21, 2020, Kuzma signed a three-year, $40 million contract extension with the Lakers.{{Cite news |last=Turner |first=Broderick |date=December 21, 2020 |title=Kyle Kuzma has new contract, still working on Lakers role |work=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2020-12-21/lakers-kyle-kuzma-season-opener |access-date=December 22, 2020}} ===Washington Wizards (2021–2025)=== On August 6, 2021, Kuzma was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] as part of a package for [[Russell Westbrook]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/washington-acquires-six-players-five-team-trade|title=Washington acquires six players in five-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}} Kuzma made his Wizards debut on October 20, recording eleven points, 15 rebounds and three assists in a 98–83 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=BEAL HAS 23, WIZARDS TOP RAPTORS 98-83, SPOIL TORONTO RETURN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100006 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On November 10, he made four [[three-point field goal|three pointers]] in the fourth quarter of a game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], including two in the final 30 seconds to elevate the Wizards to a 97–94 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2021/11/11/22775695/harrell-and-kuzma-lead-wizards-to-eighth-win|title=Harrell and Kuzma lead Wizards to eighth win|first=Kevin|last=Broom|date=November 11, 2021|access-date=November 12, 2021|work=Bullets Forever}} On December 8, Kuzma recorded 26 points, seven rebounds, four assists and hit a game-winning three-pointer in a 119–116 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |title=KUZMA'S BUZZER-BEATER LIFTS WIZ OVER SLUMPING PISTSONS IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100368 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 3, 2022, triple-double past Nets |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bkn-vs-was-0022100832/box-score |website=nba.com}} On February 25, Kuzma tied his season high of 36 points, alongside eight rebounds, seven |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100899 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 11, 2023, Kuzma scored 21 points and made a game-winning three-pointer in a 100–97 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/wizards-news-kyle-kuzma-clutch-gene-vs-bulls-has-nba-twitter-buzzing|title=Wizards star Kyle Kuzma's clutch gene sends NBA Twitter into a 40|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2023}} On June 20, 2023, Kuzma declined his $13 million player option and elected to enter free agency;{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian (2025–present)=== On February 6, 2025, Kuzma was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as part of a multi-team trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-kyle-kuzma-and-jericho-sims-in-multi-team-trade|title=Milwaukee Bucks Acquire Kyle Kuzma and Jericho Sims in Multi-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|accessdate=February 7, 2025}} He made his Bucks debut on February 7, scoring twelve points and seven rebounds in a 107–112 loss to the [[2024–25 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web | last=Stano | first=Ryan | title=How Many Points Did Kyle Kuzma Score in Bucks Debut? | website=Milwaukee Bucks On SI | date=2025-02-08 | Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mil-vs-atl-0022400736 |access-date=2025-04-20 |website=NBA |language=en}} In Game 1 of the Bucks' playoff series against the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]] he recorded zeros in points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks on 0-for-5 shooting in 22 minutes of play.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-20 |title=Bucks' Kyle Kuzma Makes Unfortunate NBA History in Game 1 vs Pacers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/onsi/news/bucks-kyle-kuzma-makes-unfortunate-nba-history-in-game-1-vs-pacers |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=Milwaukee Bucks On SI |language=en-US}} His performance was the sixth time in postseason history a player recorded zeros in every category, and drew comparisons to former Bucks player [[Tony Snell]]'s performance in a 2017 regular-season game. Head coach [[Doc Rivers]] attributed Kuzma's lack of statistics to limited action with the ball.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-19 |title=Kyle Kuzma Becomes New Meme After Historically Quiet Game in Bucks Loss vs. Pacers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kyle-kuzma-becomes-new-meme-historically-quiet-game-bucks-loss-vs-pacers |access-date=2025-04-20 |website=SI |language=en-US}} Kuzma finished the series with averages of 5.8 points, 2.2 rebounds and 0.8 assists per game with a 34.3% field goal percentage as the Bucks lost in five games.{{Cite web |title=Kyle Kuzma Stats 2025 Playoff Series Vs Pacers |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/kyle-kuzma-stats-2025-playoff-series-vs-pacers |access-date=2025-06-08 |website=StatMuse |language=en}} On December 11, 2025, Kuzma scored a season-high and game-leading 31 points, during a 116–101 Bucks win over the [[Boston Celtics]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401836747 Kuzma and Portis lead Bucks past Celtics 116-101 without injured Antetokounmpo] On March 10, 2026, Kuzma logged 33 points on 6-of-10 three-pointers in a 114–129 loss to the [[2025–26 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web|title=Bucks' Kyle Kuzma: Delivers 33 points in loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-kyle-kuzma-delivers-33-points-in-loss/|access-date=May 14, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=NBA cup champion}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nowrap|{{nbay|2017}}}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2017–18 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
